i2.speaker: tendai
i2.text: Here she is. The old borehole pump. Your grandmother's pride.

i3.speaker: tendai
i3.text: I always told myself it was bad luck. Standing here with you, I'm not so sure any more.

i4.speaker: tendai
i4.text: Three things I want you to look at: here at the pump, the tracks out on the east road, and Ruth's logbook in the office. Look for the markers on the map.

choices.text: Shouldn't we just build a new pump?

i7.speaker: tendai
i7.text: We will. But if someone broke the first one, they can break the second.

i8.speaker: tendai
i8.text: A new borehole pump costs 400. Open Build, pick the pump, and place it on the spot beside the waterhole.

i9.speaker: tendai
i9.text: We need help too. Hire a ranger from the Staff menu, and keep the books in the black—more coming in than going out—five days running.

i10.speaker: tendai
i10.text: One more thing. Mend the fence along the west side of the plains and the River & Wetland is ours again.

start.speaker: narrator
start.text: Under the pump housing, the main pipe has been cut clean through. Not rusted. Not cracked. Cut.

p2.speaker: tendai
p2.text: Saw marks. Somebody crawled under here with a hacksaw and took their time.

choices.text: Could a scrap thief have wanted the metal?

p4.speaker: tendai
p4.text: Looks like it. But sabotage needs a reason. Let's find one.

p5.speaker: tendai
p5.text: A thief takes the pipe. This one was left lying here, so the pump would look broken.

start.speaker: narrator
start.text: Where the east road meets the plains, old tyre ruts are baked into the clay. Wide tyres. A heavy vehicle.

k2.speaker: tendai
k2.text: That's not my truck, and it's no tourist bus. Those tracks run to the pump and straight back out east—never through the gate.

k3.speaker: narrator
k3.text: Pressed into the clay beside them: the foil from a pack of expensive city cigarettes.

k5.speaker: tendai
k5.text: Someone with money, and a reason not to be seen at the gate.

k6.speaker: tendai
k6.text: Could be. But nobody drives all this way by accident.

start.speaker: narrator
start.text: Ruth's logbook lies on the office desk under a layer of dust. Her handwriting fills every page.

l2.speaker: narrator
l2.text: The last entries are short. “Mr H. visited again. Third offer. Told him no.” Two days later: “Pump dead. Engineer says no fault.”

l3.speaker: tendai
l3.text: Mr H. I remember him. Tall, good suit, smiled with all his teeth. Never gave his whole name.

l5.speaker: tendai
l5.text: She knew. She just couldn't prove it, and then she got sick.

l6.speaker: tendai
l6.text: No, it isn't. But it's a name. Half of one.

start.speaker: tendai
start.text: Sit with me a minute. Cut pipe. A heavy truck that came and went without using the gate. And a buyer who wouldn't take no for an answer.

m2.speaker: tendai
m2.text: Two days after Ruth turned him down a third time, the pump died. That's not luck.

choices.text: We find Mr H. and make him answer for it.
We can't prove anything. We protect what's left.
Maybe someone wanted us to blame him.

m4.speaker: tendai
m4.text: Careful. Men like that have friends in offices. But I like the fire in you.

m5.speaker: tendai
m5.text: Wise. Water, rangers, a gate that shuts. We make this place too strong to break.

m6.speaker: tendai
m6.text: Hm. Ruth used to say I jumped to conclusions. Keep your eyes open, then.

m7.speaker: tendai
m7.text: Either way, the new pump gets a padlock, and a ranger walks past it every night.

start.speaker: tendai
start.text: The pump runs, but those three markers are still waiting for you.

h2.speaker: tendai
h2.text: The pump, the east road, the office. Click them and look closely.

start.speaker: tendai
start.text: I can't watch the whole plains on my own, {player}.

h2.speaker: tendai
h2.text: Open Staff and hire a ranger. Thirty a day, and worth every coin.

start.speaker: narrator
start.text: The new pump coughs, shudders, and settles into a steady rhythm. Clear water spills into Waterhole A.

r2.speaker: tendai
r2.text: Eight years I've waited to hear that sound.

r3.speaker: tendai
r3.text: Six a day, more than even the dry season takes. You can rest your arms now. Mostly.

r4.speaker: tendai
r4.text: It costs a little upkeep every day. Click the pump any time to see what it's doing.

start.speaker: tendai
start.text: A new ranger! Young, keen, and they brought their own boots. Good sign.

f2.speaker: tendai
f2.text: A ranger sitting at HQ protects nothing. Open Staff and press 'Zone' to send them out on patrol.

f3.speaker: tendai
f3.text: Each ranger on patrol covers a quarter of a zone. A ranger post doubles that.

f4.speaker: tendai
f4.text: Wages come out every day. If the money runs out they go unpaid, and after three days they walk.

start.speaker: narrator
start.text: Beyond the mended fence the land drops toward the river. Reeds, mud, birdsong. Water that never quite runs dry.

v2.speaker: tendai
v2.text: Your grandmother's favourite place. She used to say the river was the reserve's memory.

v3.speaker: tendai
v3.text: There's a second waterhole down there, and room for another pump if we ever need one.

choices.text: Let's bring the animals down here.

v5.speaker: tendai
v5.text: They'll find it themselves once there's water and grass. That's the trick: don't herd, invite.

v6.speaker: tendai
v6.text: Now you sound just like her.

start.speaker: narrator
start.text: Water flows. A ranger walks the plains at dusk. For the first time in years, the reserve's books balance.

z2.speaker: tendai
z2.text: Look at us, {player}. A pump, a ranger, money in the tin. Ruth would be proud.

z4.speaker: narrator
z4.text: The first is from Dr. Amara Okafor, an ecologist. She has heard the impala are back and asks to come and count them. “Herds that grow this fast,” she writes, “can eat a place bare.”

z5.speaker: narrator
z5.text: The second is on thick cream paper. Hale & Partners would like to discuss “an exciting partnership”. It is signed V. Hale.

z7.speaker: tendai
z7.text: Hale. Mr H. Well, well, well.

z8.speaker: tendai
z8.text: Hale. That name rings a bell, and not a nice one.

z9.speaker: tendai
z9.text: Whatever comes next, we face it with water in the ground and people on the fence line.

z10.speaker: narrator
z10.text: End of Chapter 2: Foundations. That's as far as the story goes for now. Thank you for playing! The reserve keeps running, so carry on managing it for as long as you like.

m2.speaker: tendai
m2.text: Watch the coin at the top. Hover over it and it shows what comes in and what goes out.

m3.speaker: tendai
m3.text: If wages can't be paid, staff start walking after three days. Better to have one ranger paid than three angry.
